supportingEvidence.title: Qatar Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Qatar PM meets Iranian foreign minister in Tehran
supportingEvidence.note: Primary Qatari source says the meeting focused on de-escalation and creating conditions for dialogue, and confirms ongoing discussion of a temporary Hormuz corridor and joint mine clearing.

supportingEvidence.title: Reuters: oil reverses higher after White House says no U.S.-Iran talks are happening
supportingEvidence.note: Reuters reports the White House said no U.S.-Iran negotiations are underway, despite Qatar's mediation effort; oil rose as markets reduced the probability of near-term diplomatic normalization.

contradictingEvidence.title: Qatar primary source confirms active mediation and a dialogue-enabling effort
contradictingEvidence.note: Active mediation means diplomatic channels are not closed; the White House statement should therefore be interpreted as absence of direct U.S.-Iran negotiations, not absence of diplomacy.

falsifier: Upgrade from MEDIATION_ACTIVE / DIRECT_TALKS_ABSENT if the White House, U.S. State Department, Iranian Foreign Ministry, or Qatar publishes primary evidence that direct U.S.-Iran negotiations have begun. Downgrade the mediation channel if Qatar or Iran says the initiative has stalled or the Hormuz corridor framework is abandoned.

evidence.title: Qatar mediation and Hormuz framework discussion

title: Qatar mediation stays active while White House says direct U.S.-Iran talks are not underway
summary: Qatar's prime minister is actively mediating in Tehran and discussing the temporary Hormuz corridor, but the White House says no direct U.S.-Iran negotiations are happening. Treat mediation and direct talks as separate state variables.
delta: Supersede any graph edge equating active Qatar mediation with direct U.S.-Iran negotiation. Current state: MEDIATION_ACTIVE + DIRECT_TALKS_ABSENT + HORMUZ_FRAMEWORK_UNRESOLVED.
firstOrderImpacts: lower confidence in immediate diplomatic normalization of Hormuz
higher short-term oil risk premium relative to a direct-talks scenario
continued value of Qatar/Oman mediation as a leading indicator rather than confirmation
secondOrderImpacts: market prices may overreact if mediator activity is misread as bilateral agreement
Nexus should model mediation, direct talks, agreement, and implementation as distinct geopolitical states
diplomatic-state classification can be tested against later vessel flow and energy-market outcomes

alphaHunter.hypothesis: Separating mediator activity from confirmed direct talks will classify Hormuz de-escalation more accurately than headline sentiment alone.
alphaHunter.baseline: news sentiment around diplomacy and oil-price reaction
alphaHunter.alternativeData: primary mediator statements, White House/State Department confirmation, Iranian Foreign Ministry confirmation, vessel flow, maritime incidents and freight/war-risk insurance
alphaHunter.incrementalValueMetric: 3-7 day classification accuracy for MEDIATION_ACTIVE / DIRECT_TALKS / AGREEMENT / IMPLEMENTATION and forecast error for physical-flow normalization
alphaHunter.killCondition: Kill the extra diplomatic-state layer if it does not improve held-out normalization forecasts versus simple headline sentiment and oil-price reaction.
